hypothesis: Retry of EXP-0010 with corrected card resolution. Setup CARD options have cardId == None and identify their card by area == HAND (2) plus index into obs.current.players[yourIndex].hand. Hand entries are Card(id, serial, playerIndex) with no .name attribute, so the name must be resolved as _card_data().get(hand[index].id).name -- EXP-0010 read hand[index].name, got None, and fell back to baseline on every setup selection. Implement ONLY the opening Active choice: when select type is CARD and context is SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON, rank options by replay priority Dreepy, Munkidori, Budew, Meowth ex, Fezandipiti ex last, falling back to existing _choose_card logic when an option cannot be resolved. expected_effect: Baseline sends Fezandipiti ex to Active on 4 of 4 offers while replays show it neutral (4W/4L) and Dreepy dominant in wins (31 opening Actives). Gate before any benchmark: a direct A/B on identical observations must show SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON choices differing from baseline. EXP-0007, EXP-0008, and EXP-0010 all passed validation while inert, so non-inertness is now proven first and screening is only run afterward.
reason: First valid (non-inert) test of the replay-derived Dreepy-first opening Active hypothesis. Context A/B confirmed the mechanism fires: 4 of 20 SETUP_ACTIVE_POKEMON selections differ, Dreepy picked 13 vs baseline 10 and Fezandipiti ex 1 vs 3. Smoke 12/20 (60.0%), screening 95/200 (47.5%, z=-0.707, p=0.480), 0 draws/illegal/crashes. The hypothesis is therefore tested and not supported: replay correlation between Dreepy openings and wins reflects deck draw, not a decision advantage, since the baseline already picks Dreepy whenever it is offered alongside worse options and roughly 80% of setup Active selections are single-option forced. Rejected rather than escalated.
